script:
Part One

My name is Hamed, and last month I attended a university open day with two classmates. We wanted to compare different courses before submitting applications. Our teacher had advised us to prepare questions, so we made a list about entry requirements, practical training, library facilities and the cost of living away from home. We also agreed not to rely on comments from strangers online when checking important information.

The first session introduced students to the engineering department. A lecturer explained that the first year includes mathematics, laboratory work and group projects. She showed us a typical weekly timetable and reminded us that independent study requires planning. I was surprised to learn that students often work together to solve practical problems rather than study every subject alone. After the talk, we visited a workshop where older students demonstrated a simple water-saving device.

We then spoke with a student adviser. She explained how new students can ask for help with course choices, study methods and personal difficulties. She also suggested checking the official university website regularly because deadlines and entry requirements may change. I wrote down the contact details for the admissions office and asked whether scholarships were available. The adviser encouraged us to compare realistic costs, including transport and accommodation, before making a final decision.

Part Two

In the afternoon, we joined a guided tour of the library and study areas. The librarian showed us how to find reliable academic sources and book quiet rooms for group work. My friend Mariam asked whether students could borrow laptops, while Faisal wanted to know about accessible study spaces. The librarian explained that equipment and support services differ between institutions, so applicants should ask direct questions.

Before leaving, we attended a short discussion with current students. They described how they balanced lectures, revision, exercise and family commitments. One student said he had initially struggled with time management but improved after joining a study-skills workshop. Another explained that asking questions during tutorials helped her feel more confident. Their experiences were different, which reminded us that there is no single perfect way to adjust to university life.

On the journey home, we compared our notes and corrected a misunderstanding about one application deadline. I realised that an open day is useful not because it makes every decision for you, but because it helps you collect evidence and identify further questions. I now plan to speak with my family, review official course details and prepare a realistic budget before choosing where to apply.
